method.value: Trace peak-intensity ridge by visual inspection on stacked-cube peak maps, excluding optically thick central region

evidence.quote: The identified filaments were also confirmed in peak intensity maps created from individual molecular transitions.

claims.hypothesis: Do filaments converge on a hub and carry large velocity gradients?
claims.experiment: Stacked-line maps, PV cuts, Gaussian and linear fits
claims.finding: Gradients are 10-100x larger than at ~1 pc scales, consistent with accretion

evidence.quote: This is 10–100 times larger than typical velocity gradients found in other star forming regions at larger scales ($\sim$1 pc).

claims.hypothesis: Can filament flows be explained by outflows or explosions instead?
claims.result: Linewidths ~10x smaller, complex-molecule tracers, curved structures

evidence.quote: which leaves us with accreting filaments as the most plausible explanation

claims.hypothesis: Will cores merge in the hub while still gas-rich?
claims.experiment: Compare free-fall collapse and infall timescales, stellar fractions
claims.finding: A 'damp' merger; Sgr B2(N) may become a super stellar cluster

evidence.quote: As a result we cannot consider this process as a clear wet merger, but as a "damp" merger.

why_this_method.value: Line stacking overcomes blending in a line-rich source

evidence.quote: Line stacking improves the signal-to-noise ratio, as well as averaging out line blendings.
Explosion events such as that in Orion KL are also a doubtful explanation since they produce clear and straightforward radial structures.

limitations_admitted.value: Line stacking may artificially broaden lines near the center

evidence.quote: We note that the increase of linewidth toward the center may be partially caused by the line stacking method.
Although our statistics are small, we see the trend that dense cores located closer to the central hub can be more massive

referee_caveats_inferred: Inclination fixed at 45 deg for all filaments, though the paper argues they differ in orientation
Mass accretion assumes the whole filament mass is infalling
Dust temperature uncertain (50-100 K) drives masses
Blackbody luminosity attributed entirely to stars
Filament tracing by eye, with no uncertainties
